sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

rows: Repair the conditional logic and semantic coverage. When operatingArea is Arctic_waters and foodWasteDischargeToSea is true, require distanceToNearestLandIceShelfOrFastIce >= 12 MI_N and explicitly encode the distinct ice-area condition: nearbyIceConcentration must be compared as exceeding one tenth (with the declared unit) and distanceFromAreaWithIceConcentrationAboveOneTenth must be recorded and paired with that condition. The current branches only check presence of nearbyIceConcentration, iceConcentration, and the second distance and therefore permit missing comparison/relationship semantics; also avoid a branch formulation that can pass by omitting or inadequately constraining applicability evidence.

Repair the conditional logic before freezing. The first sh:or branch matches merely on Arctic_waters plus foodWasteDischargeToSea=true and therefore permits the applicable case to pass without enforcing any distance or ice conditions; remove it or replace it with a genuine non-applicable alternative so applicable ships must satisfy every constraint. Preserve the existing applicability inputs without adding arcticWaters. In the applicable branch retain distanceToNearestLandIceShelfOrFastIce >= 12 MI_N, nearbyIceConcentration > 0.1 with unit:UNITLESS, and the recorded distanceFromAreaWithIceConcentrationAboveOneTenth in MI_N, with those two ice-area values on the same supplied case/ship node as the explicit pairing. Remove the needless presence-only iceConcentration constraint, since it is not a required result or independently constrained obligation here.
